body:
The padded texture update is deferred, so you'd need to defer fetching it after the initial loading (when loading the stored `texture` is set which triggers the deferred padded texture update). Before the padded texture is generated `get_runtime_texture()` returns `null` when `use_texture_padding == true` (which is by default).
```gdscript
extends Node

func _ready() -> void:
	var tileset: TileSet = load("res://new_tile_set.tres") as TileSet
	var src_id: int = tileset.get_source_id(0)
	var atlas_src = tileset.get_source(src_id)
	print(atlas_src.get_runtime_texture()) # null
	(func(): print(atlas_src.get_runtime_texture())).call_deferred() # ():<CanvasTexture#-9223372008601942514> etc.

```

I think we could either:
- Add a method like `TileSetAtlasSource.force_padded_texture_update` allowing immediate generation on demand.
- Show a warning when `get_runtime_texture()` is called in case `use_texture_padding == true` and the padded texture update is still pending/queued. Such warning would explain why `null` or an outdated padded texture (e.g. when changing source `texture` from one texture to some other) was returned.

or:
- If needed, automatically force immediate padded texture update on `get_runtime_texture()` call (making it possibly blocking).

---

+The docs need to be updated, it return a CanvasTexture now, not an ImageTexture:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/dff2b9bb66a01d8c1a207531b0752405c7399124/doc/classes/TileSetAtlasSource.xml#L52-L56
